source_claim: Non-Cancelling Intersections conjecture: any finite set union can be constructed from non-cancelling intersections via disjoint unions and complements
why_no_gate: The refutation is a first-moment existence argument. Lemma 7.2 bounds the expected number of admissible sets by E_p < 1 for p > 600 and concludes SOME marking m works; it exhibits none. There is no witness to reproduce.
The paper's own Section 9 Open Problems item 1 states that even a small-p explicit counterexample is unsolved, so no smaller instance is available either.

The only numerically checkable content, the double-counting identities in (7.1), holds for every finite point set unconditionally. Testing it would be a check that cannot fail -- forbidden by docs/GATE-BEFORE-PROVE.md.

corpus_doc_defect.detail: The corpus doc's 'Verifiable Gate / Counterexample' bullet claims a Python script validating non-existence of admissible sets in a marked plane configuration. No such gate exists in the source. This is distinct from the image-corruption seen for Tang-Zhang, Thakur and Chung-Graham: the claimed artifact was invented, not garbled.
corpus_doc_defect.internal_contradiction: The same document's ranking table row 7 lists 'Python/CPU Gate Runtime: N/A (Symbolic logic bound)', contradicting its own body section.

reopen_condition: Only if a future paper exhibits an explicit marking m, or resolves the paper's own Section 9 open problem 1. Absent that, do not write a gate.
